chapter: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
title: The cooperative band for Panama that never went
summary: Machito and Mario formed a band with Panchito Riset, Miguelito Valdes and others, rehearsed, but the Panama contract failed.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Uh Hum. Okay. When was the first time that you, that you and him played together?
Well - ah - in Cuba?
Yes.
We organized a band to go to Panama.
How old were you then?
I was about - about 17 or 18.
Okay, so that's about 1924-25, correct?
Right.
Okay. The Habanero, Bologna, all these sextetos are going strong now.
They were very strong.
Were they the inspiration for this?
Ahh - No, because what we had it was a combination that we had now in 1940. Panchito Riset was the singer.
Ah-Ha. You mean for that group that you and Mario formed?
Yeah, but he didn't appear in the picture because he was late, but I was playing guitar.....
What was the name of that group?
Ahhhh
Yeah, that was 1926, I remember the picture.
1926. Really, I don't remember, it was like a cooperative band.
I see. You were all young kids then, right?

Yeah. The only thing - the only older one was Arcelon Perez, that he lives in Mexico now, and Poligemo the bass player. The rest, Miguelito Valdes the violin --, he was about his early twanties, the rest was a bunch of young guys.
Okay. How many numbers did you have in your repertoire, in your book?
In that particular orquesta?
Yeah.....
Oh, we had about ten or fifteen.
Okay. Do you remember any of the names of the .....
Yeah. 'Manicero', naturally; we had 'Green Eyes,' we have Danzon that Antonio Maria Romeu give it to Mario, and we were helped practically everyone because Mario knew everyone.
Okay. Who were the vocalist on that group?
Panchito, Panchito Riset and myself.
Who sang the lead?
Panchito Riset.
Okay. And you sang second voice?
Yes.
And what part did Mario play in the group?
Mario was saxophone and clarinet.
Who was the leader of the group?
Mario
Mario was. Okay. Where did you work?

We worked - we was rehearsing at the a nightclub that was located where the - the owner of the nightclub was the owner of a radio station and he learned to, you know, that he want the room for rehearsal and we rehearsed about two three weeks waiting for the contract coming from Panama because we was with a group of dancers and we was the orchestra to play for them.
Did you ever get to go to Panama?
No.
What happened?
Well, one of those things, everything just failed.
